title: Headwaters dataset record
description: One published dataset: what it is, what is in it, where it came from, and where it was surfaced. Deliberately lighter than a source record - no probes, no rate limits. A dataset is a thing you might want to work with; a source is a thing you query.

hook.description: The curator's own pitch, kept in their words. This is what makes someone want to use it. It must describe THIS dataset: publisher boilerplate that recurs across records is stripped by src/quality.py, which learns it from repetition rather than from a list of known phrases.

questions.description: What you could actually ask of this data -- the field that turns browsing into an idea. Each question must be answerable from the columns this record already lists, phrased as a question, and specific enough that it could not be asked of a different dataset ('Do Canadian NHL players born in January still reach the league at higher rates?' not 'What are the trends?'). Prefer 2-4. An ingest that has the publisher's prose in front of it should fill this at the same time -- back-filling later means a second pass over the whole corpus.

subjects.description: From the controlled list in src/classify.py

sources.description: Where the data actually came from, upstream of whoever surfaced it

articles.description: The piece of writing that prompted or accompanied it

tables.description: The files that make up the dataset. Column names only - not types, not descriptions.

extra_files.description: Files in the folder beyond the tables listed - scripts, images, raw originals

found_in.description: Which aggregation surfaced it, and when. A dataset can appear in more than one.

hook_source.description: Where the hook came from. Absent or 'publisher' means it was derived from the publisher's own prose and may be regenerated by a fetcher at any time. 'manual' means somebody wrote it, and every tool here leaves it alone.

questions_source.description: Who asked them. 'curator' = the publisher's own suggested questions, which is what TidyTuesday's readme bullets are. 'generated' = written by a model reading the record. 'manual' = written by a person. Kept separate because a curator's question is evidence about the dataset and a generated one is not.
